name: agent-as-a-judge
context: Agent systems where the quality of a trajectory (all steps, tool calls, intermediate states) must be evaluated before the final response is accepted. A dedicated judge agent — distinct from the generating agent — reviews the full trajectory, scores it against criteria, and determines whether to accept, revise, or retry the response. Unlike simple output scoring, the judge has full trajectory context including reasoning traces and tool interaction histories.
benefits: Trajectory-level evaluation catches errors invisible to output-only scoring
Can judge both correctness and style/safety simultaneously
Enables automated quality gates in production pipelines
Judge reasoning trace provides explainable quality assessments
tradeoffs: Extra LLM call per evaluation round (significant cost overhead)
Judge quality depends on judge model capability
Latency increases with each evaluation round
Judge may exhibit bias toward the generating model's style
use_cases: Automated code review with quality gates
Legal document generation with compliance verification
Medical report generation with clinical accuracy check
avoid_when: Simple tasks where generation quality is already sufficient
anti_patterns: Using the same model as both generator and judge (bias)
Judge-only scoring without actionable revision paths
No score threshold — accepting all outputs regardless
design_principles: Judge and generator should be from different model families to reduce bias
Define explicit score thresholds per quality dimension
Log the judge's reasoning trace alongside scores for auditability
best_practices: Calibrate judge on a golden dataset before production use
Set per-dimension thresholds (e.g., safety must score >= 8)
Limit retry rounds to prevent infinite revision loops
references: Zhuge et al., Agent-as-a-Judge: Evaluating Agents with Agents, 2024 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.10934
Zheng et al., Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena, NeurIPS 2023 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685
